subject: 🤖 xAI Grok Bot logs into your tools autonomously, $120/seat
intro: Agents are eating software. xAI ships Grok Bot, a $120/seat autonomous worker that logs into your tools and never sleeps. DeepSeek drops a free, MIT-licensed agent framework the same week. One is closed, expensive, and ready to deploy. The other is open, free, and yours to build on. Two very different bets on who wins the agentic layer. Meanwhile, researchers proved you can predict model scaling from tiny, cheap runs. Less glamorous, but arguably the most valuable news today.

news.headline: xAI launches Grok Bot, an AI agent that logs into your tools and works autonomously
news.body: xAI just shipped Grok Bot , and it is a different kind of AI tool. Not a chatbot. Not a code helper. An AI that logs into your actual accounts and does the work while you sleep. Here is how it works: each Bot gets its own cloud computer , signs into your tools the same way you do, and keeps running after you close your laptop. No API setup needed. It clicks, types, and navigates any browser-based app like a human would. What can you actually hand off to it? The big unlock: any tool you can open in a browser is now automatable, no integration required. The catch? Pricing starts at $120/seat/month , with no free tier. It is available on macOS, iOS, Windows, and Linux today.

news.headline: DeepSeek open-sources a plugin-first agent framework under MIT license
news.body: DeepSeek just dropped Harness v0.1 , an open-source framework for building AI coding agents, and it's free to use under the MIT license , meaning you can build commercial products on top of it with zero restrictions. The core idea is simple: everything is a plugin . Instead of one rigid system, every piece of the agent, including the AI model, tools, memory, file system, and even the UI, is a swappable plugin. You can mix, match, and replace any part without touching the source code. It ships with four ready-to-use modes: Every session is fully traceable via an append-only log you can replay or fork. To try it: git clone, pnpm install, pnpm dsh web, then open localhost:3080. Expect breaking changes, it's early.

news.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 Sol at 750 tokens per second via Cerebras
news.body: You know the old rule: fast AI = dumb AI. Want the smart model? Wait for it. OpenAI just broke that rule. Meet GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast , a new speed tier for their most capable model, powered by Cerebras hardware. Same intelligence, no trade-off. The numbers: 750 tokens per second , up to 14x faster than standard processing. For context, you read at roughly 5-10 tokens per second. This thing is not waiting around. Why so fast? Normal GPUs constantly shuffle model weights between on-chip and off-chip memory, which creates a bottleneck. Cerebras keeps all 44 GB of weights sitting directly on-chip, so nothing waits. Tokens just flow. What you can actually build with this: Access is limited preview via the OpenAI API right now. You can sign up to be notified when capacity opens up.
